newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: BHP says Lennox oil, gas field back up.
newsitem.headline: BHP says Lennox oil, gas field back up.

text.p: Australia's The Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd (BHP) on Wednesday said limited production from its Lennox oil and gas operation off Britain had resumed.
Production restarted last week after replacement of a gas pipeline, but output would be limited to 10,000 barrels per day over the next three months while work is commissioned, BHP said.
Oil production from the nearby Douglas field has been unaffected and is running at 50,000 barrels per day, BHP said.
At full capacity, Lennox and Douglas can pump a total of about 70,000 bpd, it said.
Oil from Lennox, which contains high volumes of associated gas, is transported to the Douglas complex for processing.
The gas is removed, compressed and sent back to Lennox along the replaced pipeline for reinjection into the field.
BHP shut down the Lennox field in June last year when a routine inspection found faults in a big section of the original 32-km pipeline. The entire pipeline was replaced.
BHP operates and owns 46.1 percent of the Liverpool Bay development, which includes Lennox and Douglas.
